title: Score a judge's abstentions
statement: When scoring a judge against labelled cases, count every case it failed to judge or abstained on as a miss unless the case truly can't be decided.
detail: An evaluation design for a judge that answers follows, violates or not enough evidence treats the last as a deliberate abstention, reports its precision, recall and coverage, and counts an abstention on a decidable case as wrong (`uae-education-ai/EVALUATION.md`). The same design keeps an ambiguity the labels can't resolve as not enough evidence, or excludes it with a reason, rather than forcing agreement. One development case was labelled undecidable because its rule never says how many examples are enough or which contexts these learners know (`uae-education-ai/data/development_cases.json`); that label is provisional. An item evaluator's release gate likewise counts items that errored as misses, so a green run means enough of the whole set passed, not just the part that finished without errors (`icloud-work/inceptbench-main/src/inceptbench/golden/runner.py`, lines 350-353).
against: The same file's per-item stability rate across repeated runs still divides by the runs that finished without error (`icloud-work/inceptbench-main/src/inceptbench/golden/runner.py`, lines 462-463).

evidence.quote: An abstention on a decidable case is not a correct verdict.
Preserve unresolved ambiguity as `insufficient_evidence` or an explicit exclusion with a reason, rather than forcing consensus.
The rule does not define how many examples are enough or which contexts are familiar to these learners. The fragment alone cannot settle either point.
Count errored items as misses for the release gate. A green golden run # should mean enough of the whole dataset passed, not just the subset that # completed without provider/runtime errors.
evaluated = total - errors pass_rate = (passed / evaluated) if evaluated > 0 else 0.0
That is the correct conservative reading for a blocking gate; a gate cannot credit unparseable output.
